database_summary: Sakila-like DVD rental schema in SQLite. Core entities: actors, films, customers, staff, stores, addresses, cities, countries, languages, categories. Operational/event tables: rental, payment, inventory, film_actor, film_category. Many-to-many bridge tables connect films<->actors and films<->categories. Row counts indicate small lookup/reference tables and larger event tables (rental/payment/inventory).

accepted.name: film_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  title,
  description,
  release_year,
  CASE WHEN trim(release_year) = '' THEN NULL ELSE release_year END AS normalized_release_year,
  language_id,
  original_language_id,
  rental_duration,
  rental_rate,
  length,
  replacement_cost,
  rating,
  special_features,
  CASE WHEN special_features IS NOT NULL AND trim(special_features) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_special_features,
  last_update
FROM film
accepted.description: One-row-per-film canonical projection exposing film attributes and measures (useful for filtering, joining to categories/actors/inventory and calculating aggregates). Keeps original film columns and derives a normalized_release_year and has_special_features flag. | Use for: List films with certain attributes (rating, language, has special features); Compute average rental_rate or length by category or year; Filter films for downstream joins (actors, inventory, categories)

accepted.name: actor_full_name
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  actor_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  first_name || ' ' || last_name AS full_name,
  last_update
FROM actor
accepted.description: One row per actor with a convenient full_name projection for display and joins while preserving actor_id and audit stamp. | Use for: Search or display actors by full name; Join actors to films via film_actor and aggregate counts by actor

accepted.name: film_actor_link
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  fa.actor_id,
  fa.film_id,
  fa.last_update AS film_actor_last_update,
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name,
  a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS full_name,
  f.title
FROM film_actor fa
JOIN actor a ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id
JOIN film f ON f.film_id = fa.film_id
accepted.description: Denormalized bridge listing each film-actor association with actor full name and film title to simplify queries that count actors per film or list films per actor. | Use for: Count films per actor or actors per film; List film titles for a given actor or actor names for a given film

accepted.name: film_category_link
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  fc.film_id,
  fc.category_id,
  fc.last_update AS film_category_last_update,
  c.name AS name,
  f.title
FROM film_category fc
JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id
JOIN film f ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
accepted.description: Denormalized bridge listing each film-category association with category name and film title to simplify category-level aggregations. | Use for: Aggregate film counts or average measures by category; Filter films by category name

accepted.name: inventory_by_film_store
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  store_id,
  COUNT(*) AS total_copies,
  MIN(last_update) AS first_inventory_update,
  MAX(last_update) AS last_inventory_update
FROM inventory
GROUP BY film_id, store_id
accepted.description: Counts of inventory copies per film per store (one row per film_id,store_id) with total_copies measure. Useful for availability and stock reports and joining to rentals/payments. | Use for: How many copies of a film exist at each store?; Compute inventory distribution before joining to rentals

accepted.name: payments_by_customer_month
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  strftime('%Y-%m', payment_date) AS payment_month,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
  SUM(amount) AS payment_amount_total,
  MIN(payment_date) AS first_payment_date,
  MAX(payment_date) AS last_payment_date
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', payment_date)
accepted.description: Aggregates payment totals and counts per customer per month (derived from payment_date). Useful for lifetime value, monthly revenue, and cohort analysis. | Use for: Monthly revenue per customer; Customer payment frequency and recency; Cohort analysis of payments over months

accepted.name: rentals_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.rental_id,
  r.rental_date,
  r.inventory_id,
  r.customer_id,
  r.return_date,
  r.staff_id,
  r.last_update AS rental_last_update,
  i.film_id,
  i.store_id,
  f.title,
  c.first_name AS customer_first_name,
  c.last_name AS customer_last_name,
  s.first_name AS staff_first_name,
  s.last_name AS staff_last_name
FROM rental r
LEFT JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
LEFT JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
LEFT JOIN customer c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staff s ON s.staff_id = r.staff_id
accepted.description: One-row-per-rental enriched with customer, inventory, film and staff/store context to support operational reporting (rental durations, returns, revenue joins via payment). | Use for: Compute rental duration distributions, on-time return rates; Join rentals to payments and inventory for revenue per rental; List rentals for a given customer, film, or staff

accepted.name: customer_address_location
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  cu.customer_id,
  cu.store_id,
  cu.first_name,
  cu.last_name,
  cu.email,
  cu.address_id,
  a.address,
  a.address2,
  a.district,
  a.city_id,
  a.postal_code,
  a.phone,
  ci.city,
  ci.country_id,
  co.country,
  cu.active,
  cu.create_date,
  cu.last_update AS customer_last_update
FROM customer cu
LEFT JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id
LEFT JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id
LEFT JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id
accepted.description: Customer rows joined to their address, city and country to expose geographic attributes (city, country, postal_code) for segmentation and regional reporting. | Use for: Segment customers by country or city; Mailing lists or regional customer counts; Filter active customers by location

accepted.name: customer_payment_lifetime
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
  SUM(amount) AS payment_total_amount,
  AVG(amount) AS payment_avg_amount,
  MIN(payment_date) AS first_payment_date,
  MAX(payment_date) AS last_payment_date
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id
accepted.description: Per-customer lifetime payment summary (total payments, first/last payment, average payment) useful for LTV and customer ranking. | Use for: Rank customers by lifetime spend; Find high-value or inactive but previously high-value customers

accepted.name: top_films_by_rentals_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.film_id,
  f.title,
  COALESCE(rental_counts.rental_count, 0) AS rental_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(rental_counts.rental_count, 0) DESC) AS rentals_rank
FROM film f
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    i.film_id,
    COUNT(*) AS rental_count
  FROM rental r
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  GROUP BY i.film_id
) rental_counts ON rental_counts.film_id = f.film_id
accepted.description: Film ranking by total rental count across all time, exposing a rentals_rank so downstream queries can filter top-N by rank <= K. One row per film. | Use for: Find top-N most rented films; Combine rank with category or year filters to get top films by subset

accepted.name: store_revenue_running_total
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  store_id,
  revenue_month,
  monthly_revenue,
  SUM(monthly_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY store_id ORDER BY revenue_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_revenue
FROM (
  SELECT
    s.store_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', p.payment_date) AS revenue_month,
    SUM(p.amount) AS monthly_revenue
  FROM payment p
  JOIN staff s ON s.staff_id = p.staff_id
  GROUP BY s.store_id, strftime('%Y-%m', p.payment_date)
) monthly
accepted.description: Monthly revenue per store with a running total ordered by month, useful for trend and cumulative revenue analyses. One row per store and month. | Use for: Cumulative revenue trends by store; Monthly revenue comparisons and share-of-total
